name: VVIQ and TAS-20 data across five studies (aphantasia / alexithymia)
description: Pooled participant-level data from five independent studies, combining responses to the Vividness of Visual Imagery Questionnaire (VVIQ; Marks, 1973) and the 20-item Toronto Alexithymia Scale (TAS-20; Bagby, Parker, & Taylor, 1994). Used to examine the relationship between visual mental imagery vividness (including aphantasia and hyperphantasia) and alexithymia.
citation: Ruby (2025) - unpublished, Perrine Ruby, Centre de Recherche en Neurosciences de Lyon (study = "ruby")
Mas & Luminet (2025) - unpublished, Marine Mas and Olivier Luminet, Louvain-la-Neuve (study = "mas")
creditText: VVIQ item text: Marks, D. F. (1973). Visual imagery differences in the recall of pictures. British Journal of Psychology, 64(1), 17-24. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.2044-8295.1973.tb01322.x

TAS-20 item text: Bagby, R. M., Parker, J. D. A., & Taylor, G. J. (1994). The twenty-item Toronto Alexithymia Scale-I. Journal of Psychosomatic Research, 38(1), 23-32. https://doi.org/10.1016/0022-3999(94)90005-1
usageInfo: VVIQ and TAS-20 item wording is copyrighted by the original scale authors and is not reproduced here. Item columns below are identified by their official item number and (for the TAS-20) subscale; consult the source publications above for exact wording.

variableMeasured.name: study
variableMeasured.description: Study of origin.

variableMeasured.name: lang
variableMeasured.description: Language in which the study was administered.

variableMeasured.name: id
variableMeasured.description: Unique participant identifier, of the form "subj_<study>_<number>". Unique across the whole pooled dataset (not just within study).

variableMeasured.name: sex
variableMeasured.description: Sex assigned at birth, as reported by the participant.
variableMeasured.notes: Distinct from `gender` below. For most participants sex and gender coincide; the Burns study collected both constructs separately and a small number of participants (n = 4) reported a sex and gender that differ.

variableMeasured.name: gender
variableMeasured.description: Gender identity, as reported by the participant, where collected separately from sex.

variableMeasured.name: age
variableMeasured.description: Participant age in years, self-reported.
variableMeasured.notes: Missing for 3 participants.

variableMeasured.name: vviq
variableMeasured.description: Total score on the Vividness of Visual Imagery Questionnaire (VVIQ; Marks, 1973), summed across all 16 items (see `vviq_q1`-`vviq_q16` below). Lower scores indicate weaker/absent visual imagery.

variableMeasured.name: tas
variableMeasured.description: Total score on the 20-item Toronto Alexithymia Scale (TAS-20; Bagby, Parker, & Taylor, 1994), summed across all 20 items (see `tas_q1`- `tas_q20` below, already reverse-scored where applicable). Higher scores indicate greater alexithymia.

variableMeasured.name: tas_identify
variableMeasured.description: Difficulty Identifying Feelings (DIF) subscale of the TAS-20. Sum of items 1, 3, 6, 7, 9, 13, 14 (7 items).

variableMeasured.name: tas_describe
variableMeasured.description: Difficulty Describing Feelings (DDF) subscale of the TAS-20. Sum of items 2, 4, 11, 12, 17 (5 items).

variableMeasured.name: tas_external
variableMeasured.description: Externally Oriented Thinking (EOT) subscale of the TAS-20. Sum of items 5, 8, 10, 15, 16, 18, 19, 20 (8 items).

variableMeasured.name: tas_group
variableMeasured.description: Categorical alexithymia status based on standard TAS-20 cutoff (total score >= 61 = alexithymia).

variableMeasured.name: vviq_group_4
variableMeasured.description: Categorical VVIQ group with 4 levels, based on standard VVIQ cutoffs.

variableMeasured.name: vviq_group_3
variableMeasured.description: Categorical VVIQ group with 3 levels (typical and hyperphantasia collapsed).

variableMeasured.name: vviq_group_2
variableMeasured.description: Categorical VVIQ group with 2 levels (broadest split).

variableMeasured.name: vviq_q1
variableMeasured.description: VVIQ item 1 of 16, from the scene "a relative or friend you often see" (items 1-4 share this scene). Item wording not reproduced; see Marks (1973).
variableMeasured.notes: 1 = perfectly clear and as vivid as normal vision; 5 = no image at all. Missing for all 105 participants from the Monzel study, for whom only total/subscale scores were shared.
